findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-equivalent in theme to the default view: body and cards remain white with black text. The rendered CSS hard-codes body background #fff and text #000 and declares no color-scheme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and replace fixed surface/text colors with light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme tokens, while preserving tested contrast.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly with no View Transition.
findings.evidence: DOM/platform inspection found no view-transition CSS or related declarations on this MPA; the representative listing-to-detail journey performs a full abrupt document swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared card/poster/title elements, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: The long listing has no position-aware navigation or progress affordance.
findings.evidence: The layout primitive measured a 2,882px page at a 493px viewport, while DOM/CSS inspection found no sticky header, scroll-state container query, progress marker, or equivalent orientation aid.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep compact primary navigation available after scrolling and use CSS scroll-state/container-query techniques or a lightweight progress affordance.

findings.summary: An unsolicited ad-like notification obscures related content on the primary detail page.
findings.evidence: The mobile detail screenshot after 3 seconds shows a dark “This trick has women going crazy” panel over two related-content cards. It appears without user action and competes with the playback journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the unsolicited interstitial. If a transient message is essential, render it only after a relevant action with a semantic popover/dialog, clear provenance, and immediate light-dismiss.

findings.summary: The injected fixed overlay is not represented as a semantic dismissible primitive.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found a fixed 320×110 div at z-index 2147483647; the page has zero dialog and popover elements. The screenshot shows a custom close affordance layered over content.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate the third-party overlay or implement first-party transient UI with popover/dialog and declarative invoker/light-dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Reusable content cards adapt only through a global viewport breakpoint.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules or container-type; .postarticle changes from 33.333% to 50% only at @media(max-width:460px), even though the same card template appears in multiple sections and layouts.
findings.suggestedFix: Give listing regions containment and adapt cards with size container queries, retaining a viewport fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Some mobile link targets overlap or lack sufficient safe spacing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size audit failed and identified thumbnail links whose safe clickable region is reduced to 10px or overlaps adjacent card links, below the 24×24 minimum. Keyboard focus itself remained visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove overlapping link boxes, make each card one coherent link, and preserve at least 24×24 CSS px of unobscured target area with spacing between adjacent actions.

findings.summary: Analytics JavaScript dominates the page’s script cost and is substantially unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 68KiB of unused JavaScript in gtag (41.98% of 165,709 bytes). HAR shows Google Tag Manager transferred 166,041 bytes, the largest resource and about 46% of total transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics only after an appropriate consent/interaction boundary, trim configured features, and replace the full tag where a smaller first-party measurement endpoint can meet the need.

findings.summary: The page has no main or navigation landmark.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main. The direct structure probe found zero main/[role=main] and zero nav/[role=navigation] elements; only footer was present. Heading order and native focus outlines passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main> and the primary menu in a labelled <nav>, preserving the existing logical heading and focus order.

findings.summary: The representative video provides no caption track, and the listing has target-spacing failures.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found a native <video controls> with zero <track> children. Lighthouse also failed target-size on the mobile listing. Mobile reflow itself had no horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide synchronized WebVTT captions (and transcripts where appropriate) for video, and correct the overlapping mobile card links/target spacing.

findings.summary: Public pages have descriptive titles but no meta descriptions.
findings.evidence: The home and representative detail probes returned description:null, and Lighthouse failed meta-description. Raw HTML discoverability otherwise reached 100%.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, unique meta descriptions for home, listing/search, localized, and detail templates that accurately summarize visible content.

findings.summary: Home and detail templates omit canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: Direct probes returned canonical:null on both homepage and representative detail page. Robots permits indexing and advertises a sitemap, making the missing canonical signal material for this public site.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a self-referencing canonical URL on each indexable page and verify consistency with hreflang, sitemap entries, and redirects.

findings.summary: Detail pages expose JSON-LD but no social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found Article JSON-LD, but zero Open Graph meta elements; the homepage also has neither JSON-LD nor Open Graph metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url and Twitter card metadata aligned with visible content and existing JSON-LD.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers are absent and analytics cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Both 400-day _ga cookies were Secure=false and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS and nosniff; deploy a restrictive CSP; set analytics cookies Secure with an appropriate SameSite value and shorter lifetime; then verify no mixed content.

findings.summary: Tracking starts on load without an observable consent boundary and accounts for nearly half of transfer bytes.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics plus Cloudflare Insights across three third-party origins. HAR measured 177,618 third-party bytes of 361,832 total, and cookies recorded two 400-day analytics identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not initialize non-essential analytics before valid consent; minimize events and retention, batch necessary metrics, and prefer privacy-preserving first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/Trusted Types policy, or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options fallback), strict Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and introduce CSP with Trusted Types where DOM injection risk warrants it.

findings.summary: A third-party fixed layer with extreme z-index can cover first-party content.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found a 320×110 fixed div with z-index 2147483647, and the screenshot confirms it overlays related cards. It is not integrated with native top-layer semantics or page focus/state.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the injection. Keep essential first-party transient UI in the platform top layer using popover/dialog, with controlled stacking, focus, and dismissal.

findings.summary: Arabic sets lang/dir correctly but the shared CSS remains physically left/right-oriented.
findings.evidence: Arabic probe confirmed lang=ar, dir=rtl and computed RTL, but found margin-left/right, padding-left/right, left/right positioning, float:left, and border-left throughout shared layout CSS. The screenshot shows mixed-direction navigation and asymmetric section chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace physical properties with logical margin/padding/inset/border-inline properties and audit component ordering under RTL while preserving lang=ar and dir=rtl.

findings.summary: A notification-styled promotional panel uses sensational copy and appears without request.
findings.evidence: The detail screenshot shows “This trick has women going crazy” with flame emoji and “The secret no one wants you to know,” styled like a notification over the content. This disguises promotion as system-like messaging and nags during the primary flow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove disguised notification advertising. Clearly label any promotion, keep it visually distinct from browser/system messages, show it only in an appropriate context, and make rejection immediate.

findings.summary: Third-party analytics is disproportionate to the lightweight content page.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 177,618 third-party bytes, 49.1% of the 361,832-byte transfer. Google Tag Manager alone was 166,041 bytes, larger than all 30 thumbnail images combined.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential third parties, remove redundant analytics, and establish a third-party byte budget so content assets, not tracking, dominate transfer.
